arguments.premise_synthesis: The pattern day trader rule requires a $25,000 minimum balance for day trading more than four times in five days. It was created in the late 1990s because the NASDAQ could not handle high trading volumes from small accounts. Current systems can handle the volume, so the original technical justification is gone. Despite this, the rule remains in place and has caused an unquantifiable amount of damage to young and low-income investors who are prevented from day trading. This example demonstrates that SEC regulations can become obsolete and harmful, supporting the broader case for beneficial reform such as moving to semi-annual earnings reporting.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The obsolescence and harm of the pattern day trader rule supports the net beneficial effect of semi-annual earnings reporting reform.
